mainLiftTest.description: Add weight when every set reaches the top of the rep range at Solid effort or easier (RPE 8 or lower).

accessoryRule.description: Add reps up to the top of the range first, then the smallest weight jump for that equipment.

stall.description: Two consecutive sessions that fail the test: drop 10% and rebuild.
stall.message: Second miss in a row. Check sleep, food and ski load.

baseline.description: Week 1: work up to a set of 5 with 2 reps left on each main lift; train at about 90% of it for weeks 1-2. Clean: work up in doubles to a crisp, fast weight.

heavy.description: Main lifts move to 3-5 reps. First heavy-week target = last 4-6 target plus 5%, rounded to the increment (assumption, editable).

retest.description: Main lifts: work up to a 5-rep set at RPE 8-9. Also max strict pull-ups, max unbroken toes-to-bar, 5K time.

rampUp.description: Ramp-up sets before a main lift. Fractions of the target weight; empty bar first.

trim.description: Trim to fit, applied in order when the projected finish is past the cap. Cameron confirms before it applies.

timing.description: Set time = start-of-set seconds + reps x tempo (seconds per rep, from the exercise in plan.json), plus a margin. Setup seconds are added to the rest or transition before the first set of each exercise.
timing.confirmSetupDescription: Before the first set of each new block the set-up countdown waits for a 'Set-up done' tap instead of starting the set by itself. Values: block, exercise, off. The Settings toggle switches it off on the phone.

effortScale.description: The four effort buttons. Each stores an RPE number so the progression rules read the same as before.

startingEstimates.description: Rough first-session weights for free-weight accessories with no history, as a fraction of a main lift training weight or of bodyweight. Fractions for dumbbell lifts are per dumbbell; a lift marked pair in plan.json shows the total of both. Machines and cables are left blank because stacks differ. Shown as estimates; the first logged session replaces them.

dumbbellPairs.description: Exercises marked pair in plan.json use two dumbbells. Their weights are stored, shown and logged as the total of both; the weight jump is this many times the dumbbell jump so each hand moves one step.

review.description: End-of-session review: a set that was skipped, or is missing a weight or reps, is listed at the top and Save stays locked until each one is filled in or confirmed as skipped.

catchUp.note: Catch-up day: sets skipped or not reached in a saved session this week, plus whole lifts whose day passed with nothing logged. Nothing carries past the end of the week. Sets cut by Trim to fit and the if-time block are not owed.

runLog.note: Run types whose distance is not running miles. They still count as the planned run they replace.

runSchedule.note: v1.12: days a planned run can move to when its own day passes without it (0 = Sunday ... 6 = Saturday). Lift days are never offered and lifts never move. Like catch-up sets, a run still open on Sunday night is dropped, not carried into next week.

garmin.note: Which Garmin activities become runs in the log. match is tested against Garmin's activity type (lower case). type null means a run: what it counts as is settled for the week by garmin.assign (v1.12). Shorter activities than minMinutes are left out. Location fields never leave Garmin's side: the job in the private repo drops them.

assign.note: v1.12: which planned run a Garmin run counts as, whatever day it was. Clear signs first: an interval-looking run takes the intervals, a run at least as long as this week's long-run target (or longMinutes) takes the long run. Then in date order: a planned run's own day, the intervals while open (intervalMinMinutes to intervalMaxMinutes), the long run if at least longOffDayShare of the target, otherwise Easy run. A type Cameron taps is never changed.

weekRings.note: v1.14 Home rings. Lifts: a saved session per plan lift this week. Runs: planned runs done (runs.js weekRuns). Hard efforts: the Engine finisher in engineSession plus the run with id hardRun.

numberCheck.note: v1.16, Cameron Nov 19: any number that doesn't make sense is flagged for him to review before it can move the plan. A work set is flagged when a barbell weight is under the empty bar (rampUp.barWeightLb), when the weight is at most lighterThan or at least heavierThan times its target and at least minGapLb away from it, when a weight with no target is over maxLb, or when reps are more than max(2 x the top of the rep range, the top + extraReps). A set he confirms (numberOk) is never flagged again.
